source.anchor: Lee--Shen--Tian arXiv:2010.03106v4, Lemma 2 proof, Fisher-information display immediately before equation (11); used by SPHMC arXiv:2609.06906v1 Lemma 4.17
source.original_text: For the two normalized restricted-Gaussian fibers with common potential and quadratic centers y and y', the displayed log-density ratio has spatial gradient eta^{-1}(y-y'). Therefore its relative Fisher information under the left probability fiber is the expectation of the constant squared score, namely eta^{-2} times the squared Euclidean distance between the centers. In the cited proof this value is subsequently inserted into log-Sobolev and Talagrand inequalities. The selected ASTIS edge is only the exact Fisher-energy evaluation for the explicit smooth representative; it is not the log-Sobolev inequality, the Talagrand inequality, or the resulting Wasserstein contraction.

lean.statement: For every finite type iota, probability measure mu on EuclideanSpace real iota, nonzero real eta, and centers y y', RelativeFisher.information mu (fun x => 1) (fun t => -(norm (t-y))^2/(2*eta) - log (integral z, exp (-(norm (z-y))^2/(2*eta)) dmu) - (-(norm (t-y'))^2/(2*eta)) + log (integral z, exp (-(norm (z-y'))^2/(2*eta)) dmu) = eta^{-1}^2 * (norm (y-y'))^2.
